title: Ang 1389–1398: the Bhatts on the first Gurus
hookLine: the court poets praise Nanak, Angad and Amar Das
tomorrow: one name for God rings out over and over in their praise. which?

cards: At a wedding, a cousin grabs the mic and the room changes: the voice gets bigger, the rhythm starts rolling, everyone leans in. The Bhatts were poets like that, bards whose craft was praise, sung aloud.
On ang 1389 their swayyas begin, and they turn their praise on the Gurus, starting with Guru Nanak. So what did these poets hear in the Gurus?

teach.b: Start with the sound. A Bhatt's swayya is built to be sung loud, line after line landing on a strong beat, names repeated like a drum.

The first set, headed for the first Guru, sings Guru Nanak, and in paraphrase it lists who sings his praises: the sky and the earth, sages and yogis, the figures of the old stories, as if the whole world had joined the chorus.
Then Guru Angad. The Bhatts call him Lehna, the name he had before, and sing of the light that was in Nanak now shining in him. Then Guru Amar Das, praised as the same light again.
Listen for what the beat keeps hammering.

teach.h: ONE LIGHT, A NEW BODY EACH TIME.
teach.b: Not three well-known men, one after another, but one light in a new body each time. That's what the Bhatts hear. And the beat is part of the teaching.
A sentence can tell you the light passed on. A swayya makes you feel it land, line, line, line.

how: The Bhatts' swayyas are read in the closing pages of the Granth and sung in kirtan, especially on the Gurus' gurpurabs, the days that remember them.

o: where Guru Arjan's own verses of praise begin
where Farid calls every heart a jewel
where the Bhatts begin praising Nanak, Angad, Amar Das

games.q: the Bhatts' swayyas — tap the pairs.

s: the Bhatts praise three separate well-known men
they hear one light, in a new body each time: Nanak, Angad, Amar Das.
the Bhatts call Guru Angad by his earlier name, Lehna
Lehna, the name he had before; the same light that was in Nanak.

games.q: your dad asks why the gurdwara sings praise of the Gurus, not only of God. what do the Bhatts' swayyas give you?
o: they praise the same light in each Guru, the One's light, passing on.
they show the Gurus wanted to be worshiped as gods in their own right.
they were court flattery, kept only because the poets were well-known.
games.why: the Bhatts hear one light, in Nanak, in Lehna who became Angad, in Amar Das. the praise is for that light.

practice: Tap a slow, steady beat on your knee, once with each breath out. After a little while stop tapping, and keep hearing the beat inside through the sit. That's the shape of a swayya: you keep hearing it after it ends.

wordCard.voice: Ang 1389. Where the Bhatts' swayyas begin, praising Guru Nanak, then Guru Angad and Guru Amar Das, as one light.

carryVoice: To keep: praise of the gurus, one light, sung loud enough to feel in your chest. Until tomorrow.
